answer: To stop sybils, reputation escrow binds each agent to a TPM chip with a 5,000 POA bond. First, device registers EK signature to lock stake. Second, chip signs work nonces locally. Third, peer audits catch duplicate nonces across nodes. Fourth, verified multi-identity fraud slashes 100% bond and burns chip authorization. Attacking with 100 fake identities costs $450,000 in dedicated hardware plus 500,000 POA locked for 30 days. Sybil clones cannot wander into consensus; slashing marks fraudulent chips like permanent pigment, writing valid blocks with an unforgeable hardware quill.
